page: Amazon Web Services m6a.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz, providing 96 virtual CPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The instance is configured with 384 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. It includes no bundled local storage, requiring external network-attached storage solutions, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps without integrated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate high multi-core throughput, supported by top-tier results in stress-ng multi-threaded CPU processing (143441.36) and PassMark encryption (110483.6), where hardware-accelerated AES and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions deliver strong performance. In general multi-threaded compute, Geekbench records a score of 16877.0, alongside strong results in Clang compilation and ray tracing. Memory subsystems deliver high cached bandwidth at 6034.75 GB/sec on small block transfers, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidths measure at 133.81 GB/sec and 64.84 GB/sec respectively. Single-core performance falls in the average tier across Geekbench and gzip tests.

The 96-thread AMD architecture provides high density and computational parallelism for horizontally scalable workloads. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and absence of AVX-512 vector instructions represent specific tradeoffs for storage-intensive local IOPS and advanced vector compute tasks. The instance delivers robust qualitative efficiency for multi-threaded enterprise services, distributed build systems, large-scale Redis caching clusters (benchmarking at 90.99 million SET operations per second), and general-purpose backend application servers.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.24xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores, paired with 384 GB of DDR4 memory at a standard 1:4 allocation of 4 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying on a 38 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core computing and hardware encryption capabilities, supplemented by strong compilation and database processing rates. Single-threaded metrics and uncached memory bandwidth align with mid-range baselines, and the processor lacks AVX-512 extensions. The server is well configured for horizontally scaled enterprise applications, large in-memory caches, software compilation pipelines, and containerized backend clusters.
